title: Purple Team Playbook — Security Engineering Sync
body:
Meeting: Purple Team / Sec-Eng Sync — playbook synthesis and weekly triage
Date: 2026-10-12 10:00-11:00 PT
Owner / Scribe: Aisha Patel
Attendees (present): Aisha, Diego, Maya, Samir, Eleni, Jonah (observability), Priya (SRE came late)
Absentees: None

Purpose: Combine recent tabletop/pentest findings with ongoing vuln-triage and secrets hygiene work to produce a lightweight purple-team playbook we can run quarterly. Capture concrete follow-ups for vuln triage, short-lived secrets rollout, and threat-model updates for new public-facing features.

Agenda:
- Quick status on outstanding vuln backlog (5 min)
- Synthesis of purple-team tabletop (20 min)
- Secrets posture & rollout plan for ephemeral tokens (15 min)
- Threat-modeling checklist additions for public APIs (10 min)
- Action items and owners (remaining time)

Notes / Discussion:
1) Vulnerability backlog and priorities
- Current backlog snapshot (Diego): ~68 active security findings across triage board (SEC-4321, SEC-4389, SEC-4402 are high-ish). We reviewed three role-based access findings from the simulated account takeover test.
- Triage cadence: Continue weekly quick-filters on high/critical (>7.0 CVSS) and public-exposure tags. Diego to surface top-5 each Monday to #sec-eng for fast assignment.
- Temporary process tweak: tag newly opened findings with a "purple-playbook" label if they’re encountered during exercises — ensures test findings are actionable and scheduled for patch/mitigation. (Decision: adopt immediately)

2) Purple-team tabletop synthesis (Maya led)
- Recap highlights from last month’s tabletop: lateral movement via CI/CD agent credentials; exfil via misconfigured blob container; time-of-check/time-of-use race in rollout script.
- Pattern observed: secrets sprawl across legacy deploy scripts and archived S3 buckets.
- Playbook candidate workflows we agreed to capture:
  a) Detection-first scenario (compromised CI token): steps for containment, forensic collection points (build logs, ephemeral container state, runner metadata), and rapid token revocation.
  b) Recovery & hardening checklist: rotate CI credentials, add runner network egress restrictions, add job-level temp tokens with explicit TTLs.
  c) Postmortem & lessons-learned template: include specific telemetry queries to run, uptick thresholds for alerting, owners for remediation.
- Output: Maya will draft the 2-page playbook skeleton (detection + remediation + comms) by 2026-10-19.

3) Secrets hygiene & ephemeral tokens (Samir presented)
- Objective: move from long-lived static tokens in repo/deploy scripts to short-lived tokens + KMS/HSM-backed signing.
- Current blockers: older services (svc-legacy-a) still expect long-lived keys and have no token-exchange flow.
- Proposed incremental approach:
  i) Implement Vault Agent sidecar for services with CI runner support — quick win for 60% of services.
  ii) For legacy services, add an auth-wrapper (small daemon) that exchanges long-lived service principal for a short-lived token via internal STS.
- Rollout plan: pilot on staging with svc-api-gateway and svc-build-runner. Samir to own pilot; target pilot start 2026-10-25, complete pilot verification 2026-11-08.
- Mitigations while rolling out: enforce repo scanning to block committed secrets (existing GitHub App rules), add emergency revocation playbook (who can revoke, steps) — see action item below.

4) Threat modeling for public APIs (Eleni + Jonah)
- New public inference endpoint (beta) requires updating threat model templates: add sections for model-artifact integrity, supply-chain risk (third-party tokenizer libs), and rate-limit abuse leading to cost exhaustion.
- Recommended checklist additions:
  - Validate model bundles with signed checksums at deploy-time
  - Mandatory canary rollout for model version changes with traffic caps and automatic rollback triggers based on error-rate/latency/regression metrics
  - Add per-customer rate-limits and token-scoped cost ceilings at gateway level
- Integrations: link to Observability alerts (Jonah) — he will provide exact alert IDs to embed in the playbook.

Decisions made during meeting:
- Adopted "purple-playbook" tag and weekly top-5 surfacing. (Owner: Diego; Effective: immediate)
- Pilot ephemeral-token approach with Vault Agent sidecar for non-legacy services. (Owner: Samir; Pilot start: 2026-10-25)
- Playbook skeleton to be 2 pages (detection, containment, remediation, comms templates). (Owner: Maya; Draft due 2026-10-19)

Open questions / Risks:
- Legacy service retrofit complexity unknown — may require small refactors that compete with product sprints. Need prioritization with product leads (Priya to coordinate).
- Forcing revocation on many long-lived tokens could temporarily disrupt builds; must schedule revocation windows and provide rollback.
- Do we need an automated OSS scanner for model dependency supply-chain? Cost/time TBD.

Action items (concise):
- Aisha: Draft meeting summary (this doc) and publish to Confluence, notify #sec-eng and #platform-ops (due 2026-10-13)
- Diego: Add "purple-playbook" label to triage workflow; publish weekly top-5 in Monday standup (start 2026-10-19)
- Maya: Draft playbook skeleton (2 pages) and attach tabletop artifacts (logs, timeline) — due 2026-10-19
- Samir: Kick off Vault Agent sidecar pilot for svc-api-gateway + svc-build-runner (start 2026-10-25); create pilot runbook and success criteria (due 2026-10-22)
- Eleni & Jonah: Update threat-model template and provide Observability alert IDs to embed in playbook (due 2026-10-20)
- Priya (SRE): Coordinate revocation window plan with product leads and schedule a test revocation on staging (due 2026-10-21)
- Diego & Samir: Create emergency revocation playbook (who/steps/contacts) and test one forced token revoke in staging (due 2026-10-24)

Notes-to-self / follow-ups to add to Confluence page:
- Include short decision log with timestamped rationale for design choices (ephemeral tokens, Vault Agent).
- Add links to forensic queries used during tabletop inside the playbook (Kusto/ESQL examples).
- Keep playbook < 2 pages per scenario — we want it actionable in incident sheen.

Quick links referenced in meeting:
- SEC tickets: SEC-4321 (CI token abuse), SEC-4402 (public bucket misconfig), SEC-4389 (runbook gap)
- Confluence working page: confluence.redwood/display/SEC/Purple+Team+Playbook (draft space)
- Infra PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/981 (token-exchange helper stub)
- Slack thread: #sec-eng "tabletop-red-team-2026-09" (ts:172xxxxx)

Closing: Next sync to review playbook draft + pilot readiness on 2026-10-26 10:00 PT.

Scribed by: Aisha Patel
